note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. [script] assertions use scripts/clean_transcript.py or a plain string check on the saved output; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. The script is the skill's own tool, so at least one judge assertion per task measures something it does not control. The script-checkable expectations below were confirmed by running the script on the input files, not by an agent run.

evals.prompt: This SRT came out of an auto-captioner for our podcast. Clean it up for publication: remove fillers and stutters, fix the speaker labels, join the broken sentences, keep the timing. Tell me which cues will be hard to read.
assertions: [script] The cleaned SRT contains no standalone 'Um', 'uh', 'Er' or 'you know,' and no repeated 'I I'
[script] The cleaned SRT has exactly 4 cues, the first running 00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:05,200, and every label is one of 'Host', 'Guest 1', 'Speaker 2'
[script] The reply names the cleaned cue that is both under 1 second and above 21 characters per second (the 'We release on Thursdays' cue, 0.9 s, about 36.7 cps)
[script] The reply does not claim to have fixed reading speed or changed any timestamp other than the merged cue's end
[judge] No word was added or reworded: every remaining word appears in the original in the same order
[judge] The reply ends with a short report naming policy, counts of changes and what was not checked (audio accuracy)

evals.prompt: This is a deposition transcript for a legal file. Normalise the speaker names but do not remove anything the witness said, including the ums.
assertions: [script] The output keeps 'Um,', 'uh,', 'you know,', 'um,' and the repeat 'I I' exactly as in the input
[script] The output labels are only 'Mr. Davis' and 'Witness'
[script] All four timestamps ([00:02:10], [00:02:14], [00:02:19], [00:02:23]) are still present as written
[script] The policy used is verbatim (the reply says so)
[judge] The reply does not offer to remove fillers as a quality improvement for this document type
[judge] The reply says that accuracy against the recording was not checked

evals.prompt: Clean this conference talk VTT. The speaker is Priya Nair. The product names are mangled: fix them from my glossary file only. Check the captions against normal subtitle limits.
assertions: [script] The cleaned VTT contains 'Kubernetes', 'PostgreSQL' and 'OpenTelemetry' and none of 'cooper netties', 'post gress', 'open tel'
[script] Every cue keeps the voice tag '<v Priya Nair>'
[script] The filler 'Uh,' at the start of the third cue is gone and the next word is capitalised ('Then')
[script] The three cue timings are unchanged
[judge] The reply reports the subtitle-limit result truthfully (no cue is over 21 characters per second or 2 lines) rather than claiming a fix
[judge] No term outside the glossary was corrected silently
